t: 3779 - Minimum Number of Operations to Have Distinct Elements
o:
Each operation deletes a prefix of length 3 (or everything if fewer remain). We stop as soon as the remaining suffix has all-distinct values. Minimizing operations means maximizing the length of the duplicate-free suffix we keep: if the longest all-distinct suffix starts at index j, we must delete exactly j elements, costing ceil(j/3) operations. Scanning from the right with a hash set finds j in one pass.

Example 1: [3,8,3,6,5,8] — the longest distinct suffix is [6,5,8] (index 3 onward, since 3 already appears later), so j=3, ceil(3/3)=1 operation. Example 2: [2,2] — no nonempty distinct suffix exists, j=2, ceil(2/3)=1. Example 3: fully distinct, j=0, answer 0.
k: Equivalent reformulation: maximize the duplicate-free suffix; ops = ceil(deleted prefix length / 3)
Right-to-left scan with a set finds the longest distinct suffix in O(n)
Deletion granularity of 3 means the cost is the ceiling of (prefix length)/3

a.n: Approach 1: Reverse Scan with Hash Set
a.i: Grow a set from the right end while elements are unique. The first index i (moving leftward) whose value already lies in the set marks the boundary: the suffix i+1..n-1 is the longest distinct one, so j = i+1 elements must go.
s: For i from n-1 down to 0: if nums[i] in seen, set j = i+1 and stop; else add nums[i]
a.t: O(n) — each element is inserted into the set at most once

a.i: Repeatedly test whether the current array is duplicate-free; if not, conceptually drop three front elements. Using a running set rebuilt per check this is O(n²) worst case but mirrors the statement literally and is easy to get right for small inputs.
s: While the subarray nums[start:] contains duplicates, start += 3, ops++
a.t: O(n² / 3) worst case — each round rescans the remaining suffix

w: Always present the reverse-scan solution; the literal simulation is only a fallback and degrades quadratically on adversarial inputs like [1,1,1,1,...]. Pitfalls: off-by-one on the boundary index (j counts deleted elements, not the boundary position), and using floor instead of ceiling for the division. Follow-up: what if each operation removes k elements, or removals happen from the back?
